Subject: QBR: Market Signals & OKR Impact — prep note

Team —

As we pull slides for the Nov QBR, a few market signals landed this week that should change how we frame our OKR progress and risk items. High-level bullets (see attached summary + pricing compare):

- CloudBridge introduced a new entry-priced inference SKU this week (announced 11/9). Public list shows ~30% lower per-token pricing on short-context gen compared to our published hosted tiers. They are explicitly positioning for PLG churn.
- Orion-70B (open release) posted an optimized inference runtime patch; early community benchmarks indicate 15–25% lower GPU utilization for similar quality at short sequences. This affects cost-per-inference comps for mid-market customers.
- RackNexus inked a marketplace partnership with a hyperscaler to bundle inference credits with infra spend — potential channel pressure for Dedicated deals.

Implications for our QBR narrative / OKRs:
- OKR: Improve win rate on mid-market proof-of-value — we need a short competitive slide showing where we win on throughput, latency SLOs, and predictable cost (dedicated). Call out our caching/batching advantages and the rollout story for Dedicated.
- OKR: Reduce unit inference cost 12% by EOY — Maya, please add preliminary delta analysis (tokens/$) for Orion-70B and CloudBridge SKU (attached).
- Risk item: possible short-term pricing pressure — recommend we propose a trial-credits + SLA play for churn-prone accounts in the field. Markus, think through escalation path for any inbound discount requests.

Action items / owners (deadline 11/18 COB):
- Maya: update cost delta + short benchmark notes (attach).
- Markus: provide one-slide guidance on escalation & discount guardrails for the field.
- Karthik: add a 90s exec summary slide with proposed message for QBR.

Attachments (stubs): 2026-QBR-market-signals.pdf, cloudbridge-pricing-compare.xlsx

Thanks — keep it tight, this will go to the execs and board packet.

— Lauren

Quick benchmark note (attached: benchmark-notes.md) — initial datapoints comparing our hosted 13B profile vs Orion-70B (community build) and CloudBridge-S (their new SKU):

- Quality: human evals on our 13B -> Orion-70B roughly parity on commonsense & summarization (small variance on instruction-following).
- Latency (avg, 2xA100 equiv): Redwood hosted 13B: 220ms; Orion-70B community run: 180ms; CloudBridge-S (their advertised optimized path): 210ms.
- GPU utilization (proxy): Redwood: 62% avg; Orion: 48–55%; CloudBridge-S: 40–50% (their optimized runtime + shorter context sweet spot).
- Cost delta (tokens/$) at 128-token average: CloudBridge-S ~ -28% vs our published host; Orion-70B community runtime ~ -15% if customers use that runtime variant.

Recommended QBR framing (short):
1) Acknowledge the price/perf moves: "New low-entry SKUs and optimized open runtimes are compressing short-context unit costs."
2) Distinguish Redwood on: predictable throughput (Dedicated), end-to-end SLAs, and runtime features (prefix caching, KV cache) — call out a simple cost model slide.
3) Quick ask for field: emphasize a trial + SLA play and a short checklist for when to engage Sales Ops on discount exceptions.

Link to detailed notes: https://gist.github.com/maya/benchmarks-202611 (internal draft)

— Maya
